title: A coideal retraction projects relative Hopf modules onto coinvariants
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $H$ a commutative Hopf $k$-algebra, and $A\subseteq H$ a unital right coideal subalgebra, meaning $\Delta(A)\subseteq A\otimes_kH$. Use the Hopf identities, quotient coalgebra $C=H/HA^+$, quotient map $\pi$, and notion of relative Hopf module of [lem-sfb-relative-hopf-module-kernels]. Let $E:H\to A$ be an $A$-linear map with $E|_A=1_A$. For a relative Hopf module $X$, put $R(X)=\{x:\alpha_X(x)=\pi(1)\otimes x\}$ and let $j_X:R(X)\hookrightarrow X$ be its inclusion. Let $\kappa_X$ be the canonical isomorphism of [lem-sfb-coideal-canonical-tensor-isomorphism]. The formula $p_X=(E\otimes_A1_X)\kappa_X^{-1}\alpha_X$, with $A\otimes_AX=X$, defines an $A$-linear map $X\to R(X)$ satisfying $p_Xj_X=1_{R(X)}$. Consequently $1_H\otimes_Aj_X:H\otimes_AR(X)\to H\otimes_AX$ is injective, with left inverse $1_H\otimes_Ap_X$.

source.place: Bichon, arXiv:2301.05480v2, Lemma 2.6, coinvariant projection and the tensored split inclusion, specialized to commutative algebras. Read at https://arxiv.org/html/2301.05480v2; local PDF WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Write $g=\pi(1)$, $Z=C\otimes_kX$ with the diagonal action of [lem-sfb-coideal-canonical-tensor-isomorphism], and $\beta=\kappa_X^{-1}\alpha_X$. For $a\in A$, $\pi(a)=\epsilon(a)g$ since $a-\epsilon(a)1\in A^+$. Expand $\Delta(a)$ with its first factors in $A$. The counit identity gives $a(g\otimes x)=\sum\pi(a_{(1)})\otimes a_{(2)}x=g\otimes ax$. Therefore $u:X\to Z$, $x\mapsto g\otimes x$, is $A$-linear. The compatibility axiom in [lem-sfb-relative-hopf-module-kernels] makes $\alpha_X:X\to Z$ $H$-linear. Consequently $T=1_H\otimes_A\alpha_X$ and $\nu=1_H\otimes_Au$ are well-defined maps $H\otimes_AX\to H\otimes_AZ$. Commutativity of $H$ makes the given $E$ both left and right $A$-linear. Thus $F_Y:H\otimes_AY\to Y$, $h\otimes y\mapsto E(h)y$, is well-defined and $A$-linear for each $A$-module $Y$: balancing is $E(ha)y=E(h)ay$.

source.place: Lemma 2.6; Q68 explicit expansion of its projection diagram, step 1

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-coideal-canonical-tensor-isomorphism] also to the left $H$-module $Z$. Its naturality for the $H$-linear map $\alpha_X$ gives $\kappa_ZT=(1_C\otimes\alpha_X)\kappa_X$. On a pure tensor $h\otimes x$, its defining formula and the diagonal action give
$\kappa_Z
u(h\otimes x)=\sum\pi(h_{(1)})\otimes\pi(h_{(2)})\otimes h_{(3)}x=(\Delta_C\otimes1_X)\kappa_X(h\otimes x)$.
Here $h_{(2)}g=\pi(h_{(2)})$ uses the quotient $H$-action; the last equality is the formula for $\Delta_C\pi$ in [lem-sfb-relative-hopf-module-kernels] and coassociativity of $\Delta_H$. Pure tensors generate, so this is an equality of maps. Precompose both identities with $ eta$. Since $\kappa_X eta=\alpha_X$, coassociativity of $\alpha_X$ gives $\kappa_ZT eta=\kappa_Z
u eta$. Injectivity of $\kappa_Z$ now yields $T eta=
u eta$.

source.place: Lemma 2.6; Q68 explicit expansion of its projection diagram, step 2

proof.text: Put $q=F_X\beta:X\to X$. Apply $F_Z$ to $T\beta=\nu\beta$. On pure tensors, $F_ZT(h\otimes x)=E(h)\alpha_X(x)=\alpha_X(E(h)x)$ by $H$-linearity of $\alpha_X$, whereas $F_Z\nu(h\otimes x)=E(h)(g\otimes x)=g\otimes E(h)x$ by step 1. Hence $\alpha_Xq=g\otimes q$. This is precisely the defining equation for $R(X)$ in [lem-sfb-relative-hopf-module-kernels]. Since $\kappa_X$ is an isomorphism of relative Hopf modules [lem-sfb-coideal-canonical-tensor-isomorphism], hence $H$-linear, $\beta$ is $H$-linear by step 1, so $q$ is $A$-linear. As $R(X)$ is an $A$-submodule, restricting its codomain defines the required $A$-linear $p_X:X\to R(X)$ with $j_Xp_X=q$.

source.place: Lemma 2.6; Q68 explicit expansion of its projection diagram, step 3

proof.text: For $r\in R(X)$, $\alpha_X(r)=g\otimes r=\kappa_X(1_H\otimes r)$ by the formula in [lem-sfb-coideal-canonical-tensor-isomorphism]. Thus $\beta(r)=1_H\otimes r$ and $q(r)=E(1_H)r=r$, because $E$ restricts to the identity on $A$. Equality in the submodule $R(X)$ is equality after inclusion into $X$, so $p_Xj_X=1_{R(X)}$. The expression $F_X\beta=(E\otimes_A1_X)\kappa_X^{-1}\alpha_X$, using $A\otimes_AX=X$, is the formula in the statement.

source.place: Lemma 2.6; Q68 explicit expansion of its projection diagram, step 4

proof.text: The $A$-linear maps $j_X$ and $p_X$ induce the indicated maps on tensor products. On each generator $h\otimes r$ their composite is $h\otimes p_X(j_X(r))=h\otimes r$. Additivity gives $(1_H\otimes_Ap_X)(1_H\otimes_Aj_X)=1_{H\otimes_AR(X)}$. A map with a left inverse is injective: apply the left inverse to any equality between two of its values. This proves the last clause without a flatness assumption.

source.place: Lemma 2.6; Q68 explicit expansion of its projection diagram, step 5
